guidance: The long green awning over the stairs is visible from the spawn and the S-K line; the tape glints at its end over the kicker court
The spawn canopy rehearses the finishing move (ollie off a canopy end)
The way up (chevron concrete ramp with handrail) is plain but leads away from the main lines
Roof objects (AC unit; in 1+2 a textbook and stat points above it) draw players onto the roof
Bonus icons mark expert lines: three 500s on the 1,000-point gaps, three 200s on the east roof
Hidden on purpose: the pipe from the AC to the awning (obvious only on the AC) and the east roof behind the coping
designLogic: The tape hangs over the most travelled line but can only be reached from above: the series' first true visible-but-hard tape
A line above a line: roof → pipe → awning copies the stair-rail → kicker line beneath it
The spawn pre-teaches the finish (ride down a canopy and ollie off its end)
The route climbs once and then descends, so the downhill part supplies speed in a two-minute run
Three graded ways in (AC + pipe, roof-lip grind, roof to roof), the harder ones paying gaps
The tape jump lands next to K and table 2, so it costs little time; LP1 takes it first and then sweeps the letters
Failure is soft at the end (quarter pipe) and firm in the middle (climb again ≈ 15-20 s)
S-K-A-T-E is one east-to-west line with each exit aiming at the next letter
Four of five tables sit on the letter line so two tapes combine (G1 p058)
Difficulty step from Warehouse: from one jump off spawn to a climb, a descending grind and a canopy ride
Scale grows: a large campus ring after a one-room warehouse; the tape route is ≈ 3 times longer
THPS 1+2 scores and signposts the tape route (Down The Awning, Roof To Awning as AC → awning, textbook above the AC)
remakeChanges: Tape unchanged (end of the awning; AC → pipe → awning)
Textbook and stat points above the AC; Down The Awning manual gap; Roof To Awning redefined as AC → awning jump
Enterable gym with court, balance beam, textbook and new gaps
Letters on the same line; A described as above triangular blockers near the bridges
Goal objects: tables plus textbooks and wallride bells
Handicap Rail renamed All-Access Gap; Swim Team Gap absent from PS12's list; new manual and long-grind gaps
transfer: Canopy crystal: a long sloping grindable canopy over a stair-rail line from a roof to a plaza; crystal ≈ 1.5-2 m beyond and above its lower end, over a quarter pipe so a miss is a soft landing
Start the level on a short canopy whose end launches onto a grindable planter, pre-teaching the crystal's last move
One plain chevron-marked ramp to the roof next to spawn, leading away from the main line; a pickup or trick gate on the roof object
Connect the roof object to the canopy with a long descending rail; offer a harder second-roof kicker approach

Out of on-foot reach: a 4.6 m double jump plus ≈ 1.8 m body touches pickups up to ≈ 6.5 m over standable ground, so raise the crystal to ≥ ≈ 7-7.5 m or hang it over a curved transition with nothing to stand on
Land the crystal jump beside the main trick line so the detour costs seconds
openQuestions: Heights of the gym roof, AC unit and awning (estimates only)
Whether the 1999 gym had an enterable interior
Whether remake tables moved (PS12 wording differs)
G1 prints no points for Roof 2 Roof and several combo entries
Swim Team Gap absent from PS12's list
The TAS wallride onto the awning may depend on N64 collision
